name: ReShiki
tierReason: Its standalone editor combines chemical drawing, captions, layout and publication-scale vector exports.
summary: A chemical drawing editor for molecules, reaction schemes and publication figures.

license.text: Original code is MIT or Apache-2.0; third-party components retain their licenses.

engine.rendering: Iced Canvas and a shared vector scene for SVG, vector PDF and raster PNG
engine.chemistry: In-house Rust engine with native InChI and a Rust OPSIN port

caveats: CDX/CDXML interchange covers a subset; CDX can be opened and copied, but not exported as a file.
Editable Office objects require Windows; the browser omits Office integration, printing and the assistant.
Some drawings saved by 0.14.0, such as ones with a 3D model made in 0.14.0, cannot be opened in 0.13.1.

memory.method: Median summed per-process phys_footprint; descendants plus lsappinfo coalition; fresh HOME; MiB.

observations: Default JACS/ACS style: Arial 10 pt, 14.4 pt bonds, 0.6 pt lines.
Caffeine and paclitaxel received automatic SMILES layouts without cleanup.
Paclitaxel’s default layout included wedge and hashed bonds, and explicit H on two ring-fusion carbons.
Cholesterol built a rotatable ball-and-stick model from SMILES.
Default figure format was PDF; PNG export is listed as up to 1200 dpi.

builtOn.note: Own Rust canvas. All chemistry is Rust: code ported with custom changes, plus a pinned fork of COSMolKit, a Rust port of RDKit.

embedding.limit: Browser preview. One editor per page, or use iframes. Printing, assistant and Office need the desktop app.
embedding.how: Call mount(element); alternatively use <reshiki-editor> or embed() iframe.

languageNote: Python and TypeScript are for bindings and tests.

thirdParty.summary: MIT or Apache compatible code. Bundled NMR data is share-alike, ChEBI aliases are CC BY 4.0, and fonts are OFL-1.1 and Bitstream Vera.
